s4.champion: Renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension

raw.champion: Renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension
raw.rationale: The presence of a renal mass with areas of fat attenuation, visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, and a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to the inferior vena cava are highly suggestive of renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension.

rejected.label: Angiomyolipoma with renal vein thrombosis
rejected.why: Although angiomyolipomas can contain fat and potentially cause thrombosis, the presence of visible vessels extending into the renal cortex and the patient's history of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma make renal cell carcinoma more likely.

rejected.label: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a subtype of renal cell carcinoma, but the provided information does not specifically suggest clear cell characteristics over other types of renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension.

rejected.label: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary renal cell carcinoma does not typically present with the combination of fat attenuation and vascular extension seen in this case.

rejected.label: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma is less likely given the presence of fat attenuation and vascular invasion, which are not characteristic features of this subtype.
